date: 2026-09-06

description: "Upload a GeoTIFF and get an instant summary — dimensions, resolution, band count, CRS, NoData, and per-band min/max/mean. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full

Upload a `.tif`/`.tiff` file and get an instant summary of what's
actually in it — size, resolution, bands, coordinate reference
system, and the value range of each band.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

//| echo: false

{
  // Python-only tool, same reasoning as every other tool here: skip
  // writing to R's filesystem entirely so selecting a file doesn't
  // also boot webR in the background for nothing.
  mutable uploadBusy = true;
  mutable uploadStatus = "⌛ Uploading...";
  try {
    const result = await WebGeoDS.Upload.load(uploadedFiles, { languages: ["python"] });
    if (result.ok) {
      mutable uploadStatus = "⌛ Inspecting...";
      await autoInspect();
      mutable uploadStatus = result.message;
    } else {
      mutable uploadStatus = result.message;
    }
  } finally {
    mutable uploadBusy = false;
  }
}

```{.webgeods-python #raster-generate-example-py}
#| package: rasterio, numpy
import rasterio
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
import numpy as np

# A small synthetic hill (Gaussian bump), same shape already used
# elsewhere on this site for terrain-like examples (see the viewshed
# feasibility check) — one deliberately-NoData corner pixel, so the
# NoData row in the summary below has something real to show.
n = 20
xs = np.arange(n)
ys = np.arange(n)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
elevation = (100 + 40 * np.exp(-((X - 10) ** 2 + (Y - 10) ** 2) / 30)).astype("float32")
elevation[0, 0] = -9999

transform = from_origin(12.40, 41.95, 0.005, 0.005)

with rasterio.open(
    "/uploaded.tif", "w", driver="GTiff", height=n, width=n, count=1,
    dtype="float32", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=transform, nodata=-9999
) as dst:
    dst.write(elevation, 1)

"example raster written"
```

```{.webgeods-python #raster-inspect-py}
#| package: rasterio, numpy
import rasterio
from rasterio.warp import transform_bounds

path = None
for candidate in ["/uploaded.tif"]:
    try:
        with rasterio.open(candidate):
            path = candidate
            break
    except Exception:
        pass

summary = None
footprint = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}

if path is not None:
    with rasterio.open(path) as src:
        # Same convention as every vector tool: a missing CRS is
        # assumed WGS84 with an explicit warning, never silently
        # treated as "no CRS" (which would make the footprint below
        # impossible to place on the map at all).
        crs_warning = None
        if src.crs is not None:
            crs_for_transform = src.crs
            crs_label = str(src.crs)
        else:
            crs_for_transform = "EPSG:4326"
            crs_label = "EPSG:4326"
            crs_warning = "No CRS found in the file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."

        # Per-band min/max/mean, NoData pixels excluded via masked=True
        # — a band with every pixel masked (all-NoData) reports nulls
        # instead of a bogus min/max from an empty array.
        band_stats = []
        for i in range(1, src.count + 1):
            band = src.read(i, masked=True)
            has_valid = band.count() > 0
            band_stats.append({
                "band": i,
                "min": round(float(band.min()), 4) if has_valid else None,
                "max": round(float(band.max()), 4) if has_valid else None,
                "mean": round(float(band.mean()), 4) if has_valid else None,
            })

        bounds = [round(float(b), 6) for b in src.bounds]
        try:
            wgs84_bounds = transform_bounds(crs_for_transform, "EPSG:4326", *src.bounds)
        except Exception:
            # Same fallback already used elsewhere on this site when a
            # declared CRS turns out not to be a real, resolvable one —
            # the footprint just won't place correctly on the map, but
            # the summary card (native units) is unaffected.
            wgs84_bounds = src.bounds

        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = wgs84_bounds
        footprint = {
            "type": "FeatureCollection",
            "features": [{
                "type": "Feature",
                "properties": {"name": "raster footprint"},
                "geometry": {
                    "type": "Polygon",
                    "coordinates": [[[minx, miny], [maxx, miny], [maxx, maxy], [minx, maxy], [minx, miny]]]
                }
            }]
        }

        summary = {
            "width": src.width,
            "height": src.height,
            "bandCount": src.count,
            "crs": crs_label,
            "crsWarning": crs_warning,
            "nodata": src.nodata,
            "resolution": [round(float(r), 6) for r in src.res],
            "dtype": src.dtypes[0],
            "bounds": bounds,
            "bandStats": band_stats,
        }

{
    "summary": summary,
    "footprint": footprint
}
```

{
  if (pyInspect && pyInspect.summary) {
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("raster-inspect-py", pyInspect.footprint, { paint: FOOTPRINT_PAINT });
    await sharedMap.fitToData(pyInspect.footprint);
    mutable inspectSummary = pyInspect.summary;
    window.WebGeoDS.track?.("validation_completed", { tool: "raster-inspector" });
  }
}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
resetInspector = async () => {
  if (sharedMap.getGeoJSON("raster-inspect-py")) {
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("raster-inspect-py", { type: "FeatureCollection", features: [] });
  }
  mutable inspectSummary = null;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Downloads the computed summary itself (JSON) rather than a
// modified copy of the raster — unlike the vector tools, there's no
// natural "enriched" raster to hand back (the stats are page-level
// scalars, not a per-pixel value to overlay), so a machine-readable
// report of what's on screen is the closest equivalent.
downloadButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.dataset.variant = "outline";
  button.textContent = "⬇ Download";
  button.onclick = () => {
    const data = pyInspect?.summary;
    if (!data) return;
    const base = WebGeoDS.Upload.baseName(uploadedFiles);
    WebGeoDS.downloadBlob(
      JSON.stringify(data, null, 2),
      base ? `${base}-stats.json` : "raster-stats.json",
      "application/json",
      { tool: "raster-inspector" }
    );
  };
  return button;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same reactive-on-a-dedicated-mutable pattern as
// geospatial-file-inspector.qmd's statCard, for the same reason:
// Reset has nothing to re-run, so reading straight from pyInspect
// would leave stale numbers on screen after clicking it.
statCard = {
  const s = inspectSummary;
  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";

  const row = (label, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = label;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s) {
    row("Dimensions", "—");
    row("—", "Upload a .tif/.tiff file or load the example above");
    return box;
  }

  const MAX_BANDS_SHOWN = 6;
  const bandLines = s.bandStats.slice(0, MAX_BANDS_SHOWN).map((b) =>
    b.min === null
      ? `Band ${b.band}: all NoData`
      : `Band ${b.band}: ${b.min} to ${b.max} (mean ${b.mean})`
  );
  if (s.bandStats.length > MAX_BANDS_SHOWN) {
    bandLines.push(`… and ${s.bandStats.length - MAX_BANDS_SHOWN} more band(s)`);
  }

  row("Dimensions", `${s.width} × ${s.height} px`);
  row("Bands", String(s.bandCount));
  row("CRS", s.crsWarning ? `${s.crs} ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : s.crs);
  row("Resolution", s.resolution.join(" × "));
  row("Data type", s.dtype);
  row("NoData", s.nodata === null || s.nodata === undefined ? "None declared" : String(s.nodata));
  row("Bounds", s.bounds.join(", "));
  row("Value range", bandLines.join(" · "));

  return box;
}
```
